title: 2005 AMC 10B Problem 15
statement: An envelope contains eight bills: \(2\) ones, \(2\) fives, \(2\) tens, and \(2\) twenties. Two bills are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that their sum is \(\$20\) or more?

solutions.text:
There are \(\binom82 = 28\) equally likely pairs.

A sum of at least \(\$20\) comes from both twenties (\(1\) way), a twenty paired with any of the six smaller bills (\(2 \cdot 6 = 12\) ways), or both tens (\(1\) way).

The probability is \[ \dfrac{1 + 12 + 1}{28} = \dfrac{14}{28} = \dfrac12. \]

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: There are \(\binom82\) equally likely pairs of bills
A sum of \(\$20\) or more needs both tens, both twenties, or a twenty with any other bill
